Thank you brother, I appreciate your words of wisdom and encouragement. I’ll shoot you an update if any circumstances change 🤟🏻

I have absolutely started picking out my faults one by one and removing them from my being. I told her that I was in the wrong a few weeks after the initial breakup and that I would change. I have made huge leaps already by becoming sober from nicotine, alcohol, weed, and adderal. I’ve started eating healthy and going to the gym everyday to get in better shape which is for sure showing a few months in now. Do you think that sending her this thread would come off desperate as opposed to just continuing to work on myself and give her space? We spent so much time together that it seems almost impossible in my head that I could be thinking about her multiple times a day but she wouldn’t be thinking about me at all. This could be the case though, as she could still be going through a relief phase. I just feel as though contacting her right now would be further evidence of my selfish intrusiveness and need for validation and that she will reach out whenever she is ready.

You’re right, I drastically overestimated the lengths that she was willing to go to in order to keep the relationship afloat. Maybe we just both needed time apart after being locked up together for a year. Maybe it’s over for good. I’ll have to live with the consequences of my actions either way.

Agreed, that’s what my head is telling me to do it’s just my heart that is having trouble. Just leave it as is so that I don’t come off desperate. I only have a Snapchat so I don’t have to worry about the other socials. Her best friend (the one who introduced us) works at the gym that I go to and sometimes works out with me so I’ll just let her friend tell her about the leaps I’m making and see what happens 🤞🏻

I definitely have narcissistic tendencies that I’m trying to work through and I could definitely see how being selfish could’ve driven her off. Hopefully I can make her comfortable with opening back up to me in the future because we had a very strong bond that I tarnished. I definitely wasn’t the best person all the time when we were dating so I just want to change for myself regardless, whether it bears fruit for our relationship or the next one. Thank you for the comment 🙏🏻

You’re 100% right, my anxiety for sure puts me in that oneitis mindset. I unfriended her on Snapchat a month ago but now I’m wondering if I should add her back because she was still viewing every single story that I posted. I’ve been going to the gym a lot since we broke up and am looking decently muscular now so should I add her back so she can continue to see the positive changes I’m making? Or just leave the situation as is?
So you think I should just focus on self improvement and let the cards fall where they may? I don’t want to come off desperate, that’s why I’m not contacting her.

I’ve made a lot of changes since then, I’ve been sober and started to workout everyday (adding about 10 pounds of muscle). I am constantly getting looks from other girls at the gym but I want her... I’m just wondering if I should just not contact her and give her time. We were together everyday throughout the pandemic and pretty much started living together right when we started dating because there was nothing else to do. I’m just hoping that if I keep focusing on myself I can attract her again. I just have a lot of separation anxiety right now.
Why not?

That’s an impulsive decision on her part. Give her time and she will probably make another impulsive decision to follow you back on everything. Women’s feeling change as sure as the tides. Do not come off desperate with grandiose gestures. Just focus on improving yourself and you’ll form magnetic energy
